title: Using the Capabilities of an Advanced Silicon Production Line to Minimize the Spatial Footprint of BSE Detection Without Compromising Performance
content: Looking at a modern Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) from a distance, one immediately notices the numerous attachments bolted to the chamber—detectors, manipulators, Focused Ion Beam guns, and more, all crowding the microscope. Only after opening the chamber door and inspecting the interior does it become clear that most of these attachments are directed at a single point, the sample location. This is where the electron beam interacts with the specimen, generating all the relevant data. For most detectors the following applies: the more signal captured, the better the detector's performance. However, this directly implies that several detectors and attachments compete for space next to the polepiece and around the sample. Thus, reducing the space requirement for any of these detectors will create room for other detectors and devices, enabling simultaneous use and gaining more information from each scan. Here we focus on minimizing the footprint of the Back Scattered Electron (BSE) Detector while keeping its performance on the same level. This is done by using a dedicated Silicon detector fabrication line with the freedom of freely choosing the design and layout of the Silicon based Diodes.
